senses.example: Her vivid story made me feel like I could see the orange cliffs.

senses.definition: The words someone knows or uses, or the words used for a certain subject or language.
senses.example: We made a vocabulary list before reading about the ocean.

senses.definition: A speech sound made with air flowing freely through the mouth, or a letter used to write such a sound.
senses.example: The word map has a vowel sound between two consonants.

senses.definition: A piece of cooked batter with a pattern of little squares from the pan it was cooked in.
senses.example: I filled the squares of my waffle with berries.

senses.definition: To have trouble making up your mind or keep changing your choice.
senses.example: We waffled between going to the zoo and riding bikes.

senses.definition: A cart with four wheels for carrying things, sometimes pulled by hand or by an animal.
senses.example: We pulled the books across the room in a little red wagon.

senses.definition: A nut with a hard, rough shell, or the tree that grows it.
senses.example: The squirrel carried a walnut across the yard.

senses.definition: A thin stick used for a task or held to perform magic in a story.
senses.example: We used a wand to blow soap bubbles.

senses.definition: An insect related to bees and ants, often with a narrow middle. Some wasps can sting.
senses.example: A wasp flew past us and landed on a leaf.

senses.definition: A place where a stream or river falls over a steep drop.
senses.example: Mist rose where the waterfall hit the pool.

senses.definition: Made to keep water from passing through.
senses.example: I put my map in a waterproof pouch before getting in the canoe.

senses.definition: To change, coat, or seal something so water cannot pass through it.
senses.example: We waterproofed the seams on the canvas shelter.

senses.definition: A solid material that can be soft or melt when warmed, used for candles and protective coatings.
senses.example: A drop of melted wax hardened on the candleholder.

senses.definition: To rub or cover a surface with wax.
senses.example: We waxed the wooden table so the surface would shine.

senses.definition: To increase, especially when the lit part of the Moon that we see is growing.
senses.example: We watched the Moon wax over the week.

senses.definition: A net of threads made by a spider, or a similar network of connected things.
senses.example: We saw a web stretched across the corner.

senses.definition: The part of the internet that lets people open connected pages, often called the Web.
senses.example: I used the web to find the library’s hours.

senses.definition: A day from Monday to Friday.
senses.example: On a weekday, our street is busiest at the start of school.

senses.definition: Saturday and Sunday, or the break around those days.
senses.example: We went to the fair over the weekend.

senses.definition: To cry and let tears come out of your eyes.
senses.example: The child began to weep when she saw the broken kite.

senses.definition: Very strange or unexpected.
senses.example: A weird squeaking sound came from the closet.

senses.definition: A small cart, usually with one wheel and two handles, for carrying things such as soil or tools.
senses.example: We pushed a wheelbarrow full of leaves to the compost pile.

senses.definition: Every time something happens, or at any time that it happens.
senses.example: Whenever we pass the pond, we look for frogs.

senses.definition: In any place someone goes or something happens, or in every such place.
senses.example: We saw wet leaves wherever the path went under trees.

senses.definition: A period of time that is usually not exact.
senses.example: I waited a while for the concert to begin.

senses.definition: During the time that another thing happens.
senses.example: I carried the food while Maya found a table.

senses.definition: Used to show a difference between two things.
senses.example: Our old bus had green seats, while the new one has blue ones.

senses.definition: A kitchen tool with thin loops or wires used for beating or mixing food.
senses.example: We used a whisk to take the lumps out of the batter.

senses.definition: To beat or mix something with quick strokes.
senses.example: Whisk the eggs in the bowl before pouring them into the pan.

senses.definition: To move or take someone or something somewhere very quickly.
senses.example: A gust whisked the paper across the playground.

senses.definition: A plant with flowers that grows without being planted or cared for by people.
senses.example: A yellow wildflower grew at the edge of the trail.

senses.definition: A kind of tree or shrub that often grows near water and has narrow leaves.
senses.example: Long branches from the willow hung over the pond.

senses.definition: A machine with large blades that turn in the wind to do work such as grinding grain or pumping water.
senses.example: The old windmill once ground flour for the town.

senses.definition: An opening in a wall or vehicle, often covered by glass, through which light passes or people can see.
senses.example: The window gave us a view of the rain.

senses.definition: One framed area on a computer screen that shows a program, document, or other activity.
senses.example: I opened a new window to look up the bus schedule.

senses.definition: A limited time when something can happen.
senses.example: The rain gave us a short window of dry weather to play outside.

senses.definition: The ability to use what you know and have learned to make careful choices.
senses.example: Our guide had the wisdom to turn back before the storm reached the ridge.

senses.definition: Giving a lot of pleasure, interest, or delight.
senses.example: We had a wonderful day exploring the tide pools.

senses.definition: Made of wood.
senses.example: Two wooden boats sat beside the dock.

senses.definition: Stiff or showing little feeling.
senses.example: The puppet gave a wooden smile as the curtain opened.

senses.definition: A piece of paper, foil, or other thin material put around something to cover or protect it.
senses.example: I picked up the empty wrapper from the bench.

senses.definition: The joint that joins the hand to the arm.
senses.example: I wore a blue band around my wrist.

senses.definition: A type of radiation that can pass through some materials, or a picture made with it.
senses.example: The doctor showed us an X-ray where the bones appeared pale.

senses.definition: To make a picture of the inside of something using this type of radiation.
senses.example: The dentist X-rayed my teeth to check below the surface.

senses.definition: A musical instrument with wooden bars of different lengths that make different notes when struck.
senses.example: I played three notes on the xylophone.

senses.definition: An outdoor area beside a building that may be used for playing, working, or growing plants.
senses.example: We kicked a ball around the yard.

senses.definition: A unit of length equal to three feet.
senses.example: The ribbon was almost one yard long.

senses.definition: A long strand of fibers used for knitting, weaving, or other kinds of cloth work.
senses.example: A ball of red yarn rolled across the floor.

senses.definition: A long story, often one with surprising events or made-up parts.
senses.example: Grandpa likes to tell a yarn about his first fishing trip.

senses.definition: On the day before today.
senses.example: I returned that book yesterday.

senses.definition: The day before today, or the past more generally.
senses.example: Yesterday was the first day of camp.

senses.definition: A toy made of joined disks with a string that winds around the middle so it can travel up and down.
senses.example: I practiced letting the yo-yo spin at the end of the string.

senses.definition: A bluish-gray metal often used to protect steel from rust, also needed in small amounts by living things.
senses.example: The screws had a thin coating of zinc.

senses.definition: A long, usually green summer squash with soft skin when picked young.
senses.example: We sliced the zucchini and cooked it with tomatoes.
